newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada March wage settlements average 1.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Canada March wage settlements average 1.6 pct.

text.p: Annual wage increases in Canadian collective bargaining agreements reached in March averaged 1.6 percent, up fractionally from a revised 1.5 percent (1.2 percent) in February, the Department of Human Resources Development said on Thursday.
For the first quarter of 1997, wage settlements averaged 1.5 percent annually, down slightly from the 1.6 percent figure in the previous quarter but up from the 1996 aggregate average of 0.9 percent.
A Reuters survey of economists had forecast 1.2 percent annual average wage increases for March.
The department released the following figures for March:

Wage increases are the average annual percentage increase in base rates -- the wage rate of the lowest paid classification in a bargaining unit -- over the term of the agreement in settlements negotiated during the period shown.
The 1.6 percent public sector figure was up from February's revised 1.0 percent and much higher than January's 0.2 percent.
In the private sector, March's 1.7 percent climb was down from 2.1 percent in February and 2.2 percent in January.
